clue.text: Courage and audacity needed for such an obstruction

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
neck is informal for cheek or audacity, as in 'what a neck!'

explanation.surface: Getting past some blockage apparently calls for both nerve and cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are British slang: 'bottle' is courage, 'neck' is brazen cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow point where traffic or progress is held up is the standard sense of the word.

clue.text: I must have short party up in tropical resort

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the clipped word is read from bottom to top
short says the party's name loses its tail end

parts.note: Labour is one of the main UK political parties

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker insists on a quick celebration at a sunny destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts LABOUR to LAB, and 'up' turns it into BAL, followed by I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indonesian island is a famous beach holiday destination in the tropics.

clue.text: Shoot number, with military exercise almost completed

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: almost completed says the exercise stops just short of its final letter

parts.note: drill is parade-ground training for soldiers

explanation.surface: A firing count for soldiers whose training is nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost completed' trims DRILL to DRIL. 'Shoot' looks like a gun order but is a plant's growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is a slender climbing shoot that a plant sends out to cling on.

clue.text: I fill chamber half up: stirring everything, to produce this wine

indicators.note: stirring mixes up all the letters gathered, so they are rearranged together
half of the two-letter word up is its first letter

explanation.surface: Instructions for pouring something into a vessel and mixing it to make a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes U from 'up'; 'stirring everything' rearranges I, FILL, CHAMBER and U together.
explanation.definitionFit: Liebfraumilch is a sweet German white wine, once hugely popular in Britain.

clue.text: Most horrible November so far is equal on temperature

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
so far, as in 'so far as I know', can be put as 'as far', giving as
ties means is level or equal with

explanation.surface: A weather report: this November is the worst yet, temperatures matching records.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastiest is the superlative of nasty, meaning most unpleasant or horrible.

clue.text: With no energy input, make packing case

indicators.note: with no says the letter for energy is taken away from the word

parts.note: create means make
E is the physics symbol for energy, here the letter put inside

explanation.surface: An energy-free way of producing a box for shipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no' removes E from inside CREATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A crate is a wooden box used for packing and transporting goods.

clue.text: Not very many spotted in safe waters

indicators.note: spotted in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only a handful of something were sighted in calm seas.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a small number, the same as 'not very many'.

clue.text: Roll up on opening of Goodwood to get the measure of horse races

parts.note: to furl a flag or sail is to roll it up

indicators.note: opening of points to the first letter of the racecourse name

explanation.surface: Rolling up at the start of the Goodwood meeting to size up the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Goodwood is an English racecourse in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlong, an eighth of a mile, is the unit used to state race distances.

clue.text: Poet whose writings have value?

parts.note: words means things written
worth means value

explanation.surface: Asks which poet's writings are worth anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet's surname splits into a playful claim about his own verse.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was the English Romantic poet of the Lake District.

clue.text: Netting wrapped round knight's weapon

indicators.note: wrapped round says the fabric encloses the letter for the knight

parts.note: lace is fine openwork fabric, a kind of netting
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight's weapon covered with mesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapped round' puts N inside LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is the long spear carried by a mounted knight.

clue.text: Blustering type mangled reggae in small western resort, initially

indicators.note: in says the shuffled letters sit inside the other pieces
initially points to the first letter of the word resort
mangled says the music's letters are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: A braggart murders some reggae at a little seaside town in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like the setting but only gives its first letter; 'mangled' is the anagram signal and 'in' places the result between S W and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A swaggerer is someone who struts and boasts, a blustering show-off.

clue.text: Protective figure's financier for a rival daily?

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: The Guardian is a British daily paper, a rival of the Telegraph
an angel is someone who backs a theatre production with money

explanation.surface: Asks whether a protector is really the money behind a competing newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is a rival of the Telegraph, where this clue appeared; an 'angel' is theatre slang for a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel is a spirit believed to watch over and protect a person.

clue.text: Not entirely sorry, with great fire raging, to find cool things

indicators.note: raging says the letters are thrown about wildly and rearranged
not entirely says the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone half-apologetic about a huge blaze looks for ways to cool down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' cuts SORRY to SORR; 'raging' rearranges that with GREAT FIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fridges are appliances whose job is to keep food chilled.

clue.text: Official foolishly directed to support a Conservative

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it
foolishly says the word's letters are put together in a silly, jumbled way

explanation.surface: A civil servant blunderingly sent to back up a Tory politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' rearranges DIRECTED to CREDITED, which goes 'to support' (below) A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Accredited means officially recognised or authorised.

clue.text: Fall down in mountain pass and expire

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountain peaks
a policy or right that lapses expires

explanation.surface: A climber slips in the pass and dies.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to fall down or give way suddenly.

clue.text: Woman partnered with serviceman, getting old quite slowly

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A woman paired with a soldier, both ageing at a gentle pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction for a slow tempo, slower than andante.

clue.text: Animal's relative used to make a soldier's headgear?

parts.note: bear's, belonging to the animal
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Asks whether a creature's relation was used to make a guardsman's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The tall fur hats are worn by the guards outside Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearskin is the tall black fur cap of British Guards regiments.

clue.text: Rush ahead of me to find flower arrangement

parts.note: to race is to rush

explanation.surface: A florist is urged to hurry ahead and find a bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower arrangement' is botanical: how flowers sit on a stem, not a vase display.
explanation.definitionFit: A raceme is a flower cluster with stalked flowers along one central stem.

clue.text: Smoke coming from revolutionary base

parts.note: Che Guevara is the famous Argentine-born revolutionary
a root is a base or foundation

explanation.surface: Smoke rising from a rebel stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar cut square at both ends, something to smoke.

clue.text: Potty scientist maybe mistreated rats and mice

indicators.note: mistreated says the animals' letters are handled roughly and rearranged

explanation.surface: A deranged lab scientist cruelly abuses rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like 'mad' but means one who makes pots; 'maybe' marks a fanciful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceramist works with pottery, so could whimsically be called a scientist of pots.

clue.text: Six-footers in religious groups?

parts.note: sects are religious groups

explanation.surface: Asks whether tall people are to be found among religious bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footers' suggests tall people; it means creatures with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, so they are literally six-footers.

clue.text: This opera may be something to see in a German cave!

definitions.text: This opera may be something to see in a German cave!

parts.words: This opera may be something to see in a German cave
parts.note: the opera's German title means 'the bat', a creature found in caves

explanation.walkthrough: The Johann Strauss operetta's title translates as 'The Bat'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Strauss operetta's German title literally names a cave-dwelling flying mammal.

clue.text: Ride around top of road: it's not so wet

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about into a new order
in a down clue, top of points to the first letter of road

explanation.surface: Cycling about at the head of the road, where the surface is less soggy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal but here rearranges the letters; 'top of road' then adds R.
explanation.definitionFit: Drier is the comparative of dry, meaning less wet.

clue.text: Left harbour

definitions.meaning: the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A ship has departed from the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, port means the left side; a port is also a harbour.

clue.text: Blast husband going to choose dental accessory

parts.note: a toot is a blast on a horn
to pick is to choose

explanation.surface: An exasperated wife says 'blast!' as her husband goes off to make a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothpick is a small stick for cleaning between the teeth.

clue.text: Small creature producing grand repeated sound, as we may hear it

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: as we may hear it says the letters are spelt as the word is spoken

parts.note: an echo is a sound repeated back

explanation.surface: A tiny animal making a big resonating noise, judging by what we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: ECHO said aloud gives the ending, spelt ECKO.
explanation.definitionFit: A gecko is a small lizard, named for its clicking call.

clue.text: Information that a doctor is holding back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read in reverse
holding says the words contain the letters needed

explanation.surface: Facts that a GP is keeping to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: ATAD hides in 'thAT A Doctor'; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures, a synonym for information.

clue.text: Composer in far off New Zealand heard programme

indicators.note: off says the letters of far are rearranged
heard says the word is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a list is a programme or schedule of items

explanation.surface: A composer's work picked up on the radio in distant New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges FAR into FRA; LIST 'heard' gives LISZT.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian Romantic pianist and composer.
